questions.question: Why do freelancers build their own invoicing tools instead of using existing software?
questions.answer_summary: A recurring pattern on Hacker News: freelancers report existing invoicing platforms are 'overly complex and expensive' for solo, multi-currency needs, leading them to build minimal personal tools (e.g., a 100-line CLI) or ship small products like Invoroo and PlainInvoice specifically to solve this.

questions.question: What lightweight tools exist for freelancers who need multi-currency invoices without hiring an accountant?
questions.answer_summary: Community-built examples include Invoroo (minimal multi-currency/multi-language invoicing), klirr (open-source, Rust-based, automates exchange-rate conversion and emailing of invoices), and PlainInvoice (no-login instant invoice generation with multi-currency support).

questions.question: How do freelancers in countries with restricted banking access get paid by international clients?
questions.answer_summary: A discussed real-world example is a Venezuelan freelance programmer who found getting paid in Bitcoin 'orders of magnitude easier than any other alternative' because of banking/currency restrictions in his country — illustrating that in some markets, the 'without an accountant' problem is really a 'without normal banking access' problem.

questions.question: Are there invoicing tools built specifically for informal/chat-based markets rather than desktop software?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — a WhatsApp-based invoicing bot was built specifically to help freelancers and informal businesses in markets like Nigeria, India, Brazil, and Southeast Asia create/track invoices inside a chat interface rather than a traditional web app.

questions.question: What's the practical difference between just converting currency for display vs actually reconciling multi-currency income for taxes?
questions.answer_summary: Not directly answered by a single source, but implied across multiple tool-building threads: makers focus on generating the invoice and converting the shown amount (exchange-rate math), while the harder downstream problem of tax/bookkeeping reconciliation across currencies is largely left unaddressed by these DIY tools — a genuine content gap.

questions.question: Why do freelancers avoid mainstream invoicing platforms like FreshBooks/QuickBooks for simple multi-currency needs?
questions.answer_summary: Reported motivation across several Show HN/Ask HN threads is cost and complexity mismatch — solo freelancers don't want subscription-priced, feature-heavy accounting suites just to send a few invoices in different currencies each month.
